# ASC OS — Build Specification

## Epics, user stories, acceptance criteria and flows

Oct 7, 2026 · Owner @Anurag Chatterjee · Companion to the ASC OS Requirements Document

## 1. How to use this document

Two documents, two jobs. The Requirements Document says what the product is and why. This one says what gets built, in what order, and how you know it is done.

| Question | Document |
| --- | --- |
| Why does the system do this? | Requirements, by section |
| What exactly must the code do? | This document, by story |
| How do I know the story is finished? | Acceptance criteria in this document |
| What do I build first? | Epic map, section 3 |

A developer picking up a ticket reads the story and its acceptance criteria here, and opens the referenced requirements section when they need the reasoning.

### ID scheme

| Prefix | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-n | A section of the Requirements Document | REQ-8 is Financial clearance |
| EP-X | An epic, lettered A to M | EP-D is Financial clearance |
| US-X-nn | A user story inside that epic | US-D-03 |
| AC-X-nn-n | An acceptance criterion on that story | AC-D-03-2 |
| NFR-n | A non-functional criterion from section 20 | NFR-4 |

Story IDs are permanent. If a story is dropped, its ID is retired, never reused. Put the story ID in the branch name, the commit message and the PR title so a change can be traced back to a requirement without archaeology.

### Acceptance criteria format

Criteria are written in Given / When / Then. This is not ceremony — each criterion maps to one automated test, and a criterion that cannot be written this way is usually a requirement that has not been thought through yet.

AC-D-03-1  
Given a case with an authorization approved for 12 Nov to 12 Dec  
When the case is rescheduled to 15 Dec  
Then the authorization check moves to failed  
And a work item of type auth\_revalidation is created for the financial clearance role  
And the case readiness becomes blocked

### What a story does not contain

No UI layout, no component names, no table or column names, no framework choices. Those are the developer's. A story says what must be true after the user acts; it does not say which button they pressed.

The exception is where a specific behaviour is clinically or legally required — an immutable signature, a hard gate, a logged override. Those are stated as requirements because getting them wrong has consequences outside the codebase.

### Status

Every story here is **Draft** until reviewed by Anurag. Stories touching coding, quality measures or regulatory behaviour need a second review by someone with current credentials before they enter a sprint. The twelve open questions in REQ-22 block specific epics; those are marked where they land.

## 2. Personas and journeys

### Personas

| Persona | Who | Context of use | What makes them abandon the system |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Dr. R — endoscopist** | GI physician, owner | Standing, gloved, dim room, 90 seconds between cases, 12 cases a block | Any screen that takes more than two taps; being asked to confirm something he already said |
| **Nina — pre-op nurse** | RN, 10 years | Seated at a bay terminal, interrupted constantly, 8 patients at once | Losing work on interruption; re-entering data the referral already contained |
| **Carl — circulator** | RN in the room | Standing, gloved, one hand, watching the patient | Anything requiring a keyboard during a case |
| **Rosa — front desk** | Non-clinical | Desk, phone ringing, patient standing in front of her | Not being able to answer "what do I owe today?" |
| **Dee — financial clearance** | Biller, part-time | Batch work, desk, deep payer knowledge | A worklist that does not tell her what to do next |
| **Mo — coder / biller** | Certified coder, remote | Batch work, end of day | Code suggestions she cannot audit back to the note |
| **Ana — administrator** | Runs the center | Desk, reporting, survey prep | Not being able to produce evidence for a surveyor |
| **Patient** | Mostly 45+, screening | Phone, at home, anxious, often with poor health literacy | Any portal requiring a password to see their prep instructions |

### Journey 1 — the screening patient, end to end

Fax arrives from the referring PCP. Extraction reads it, matches the patient, creates the case as requested. Nina triages: accept. Rosa calls, offers a date in Dr. R's Tuesday block, books it.

The financial agent runs eligibility, finds Aetna active, pulls benefits, determines no auth required for screening, computes the estimate at zero because the screening benefit applies. The outreach agent sends prep instructions and the prescription goes to the pharmacy.

Seven days out, eligibility re-runs. Five days out, Nina calls: medications, anticoagulants — none, allergies, escort confirmed. Two days out, prep reminder. Day before, confirmation with arrival time and NPO.

Day of: Rosa checks in, verifies identity, nothing to collect. Nina does vitals, IV, H&P update, Dr. R signs it. Carl runs the timeout. Dr. R scopes, speaks findings, two polyps removed. Carl labels two specimens. PACU, Aldrete, discharge with instructions, escort confirmed.

Dr. R reviews the drafted note, corrects one size, signs. Codes suggested with modifier PT because screening became therapeutic; Mo reviews, approves. Claim goes out next morning. Pathology returns in four days — tubular adenomas, low grade. Dr. R acknowledges, confirms a seven-year interval, patient notified by letter. Recall register holds the date.

**That journey is the system.** Every epic below is a piece of it.

### Journey 2 — the case that nearly fails

Same start. At the five-day call the patient mentions clopidogrel that the referral never listed. The anticoagulation check fails, readiness goes blocked, a work item goes to Nina. She contacts the cardiologist, gets a five-day hold instruction, records it. The procedure date is four days out — too soon. Rosa reschedules to the following week.

On reschedule, the authorization check revalidates automatically and the pre-op timeline recomputes. Prep instructions reissue with the new date and a new second-dose time.

**Every blocked path in this document is a variant of this journey.** The system's job is to find the problem on day five, not in the bay.

### Journey 3 — the result that nearly disappears

Two specimens go to the lab. One result returns in four days and matches on container label. The second does not return. At day six the open-specimen register escalates to Ana, who calls the lab: the jar was received but mislabelled. Result arrives day eight, unmatched, lands in the human queue, Mo matches it manually. It reads high-grade dysplasia. The flag routes to Dr. R within the hour, he acknowledges, the surveillance interval reopens as a work item and shortens, and the patient gets a phone call rather than a letter.

**This journey is why EP-H exists.** Build it as if it will happen, because it will.

## 3. Epic map and release plan

Thirteen epics. The dependency column is what determines order — an epic cannot start before its dependencies are usable, not merely designed.

| EP-D | Financial clearance | 8 | EP-A, EP-C | 12 | 2 |
| EP-E | Pre-operative readiness | 9 | EP-C | 11 | 2 |
| EP-F | Day of surgery | 10 | EP-E | 13 | 3 |
| EP-G | Clinical documentation | 11 | EP-F | 10 | 3 |
| EP-H | Specimens and pathology | 12 | EP-G | 9 | 3 |
| EP-I | Inventory, scopes, reprocessing | 13 | EP-A | 8 | 3 |

### Release plan

Phases map to the go-live plan in REQ-21. Dates assume a January opening; adjust the anchor, keep the ordering.

| Phase | Epics | Target | Gate to exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EP-A, EP-B, EP-C | 6 weeks before opening | A referral can become a scheduled case, end to end, with real staff |
| 2 | EP-D, EP-E | 4 weeks before | A scheduled case reaches ready without manual intervention |
| 3 | EP-F, EP-G, EP-H, EP-I | 2 weeks before | Dry run 3 runs clean from check-in to signed note and labelled specimen |
| 4 | EP-J, EP-K | Opening week | First claim submitted and accepted at 277CA within 7 days of first case |
| 5 | EP-L | Within 30 days | ASCQR data captured from day one, reportable |

### EP-M is not a phase

The agent layer ships alongside the epic it automates, never ahead of it. Build the manual path first, then automate it. A financial clearance agent with no working manual clearance screen has nothing to fall back to when it abstains, and it will abstain.

The one exception is document extraction in EP-B, which has no sensible manual equivalent — nobody is going to key a fax by hand at volume. That ships with EP-B.

### What slips first

If the schedule compresses, cut in this order: ambient capture in EP-G (physicians type), patient self check-in in EP-F (front desk does it), cost-per-case reporting in EP-I, and the agent layer in EP-D (staff work the queue manually).

Do not cut: anything in EP-A, the specimen loop in EP-H, the hard gates in EP-F, or the physician code approval in EP-J. Those are either safety or legal.

### Capacity note

Thirteen epics and roughly 130 stories against a team of two engineers plus an intern, with a fixed opening date. At a conservative three stories per engineer-week, phases 1 to 3 alone are about 20 engineer-weeks. Count the weeks available before committing to the date, and if the arithmetic does not work, the honest move is to cut scope now using the list above rather than discover it in December.

## 4. Conventions, Definition of Ready, Definition of Done

### Story template

US-D-03 — Revalidate authorization on reschedule [EP-D] [REQ-8]  
  
As a financial clearance specialist  
I want the system to recheck authorization validity whenever a case moves  
So that a rescheduled case does not go to theatre on a lapsed auth  
  
Priority: Must Estimate: 3 Phase: 2  
Depends on: US-D-01, US-C-04  
  
Acceptance criteria  
 AC-D-03-1 Given / When / Then  
 AC-D-03-2 ...  
  
Out of scope  
 - Submitting a new auth request (US-D-04)  
  
Notes  
 - Blocked by REQ-22 open question 6 (clearinghouse)

Priority uses MoSCoW: **Must** means the center cannot open without it. Be strict — if everything is Must, the list carries no information. Estimates are Fibonacci points; anything above 8 gets split before it enters a sprint.

### Definition of Ready

A story enters a sprint only when all of these hold:

* ☐ Acceptance criteria written in Given / When / Then, each independently testable
* ☐ Dependencies identified and either done or in the same sprint
* ☐ No unresolved REQ-22 open question blocks it
* ☐ Test data available — a synthetic patient, a sample 271, a sample fax
* ☐ Clinical or regulatory content reviewed by Anurag where the story touches it
* ☐ Estimated by whoever will build it
* ☐ The developer can state what "done" looks like without re-reading the story

### Definition of Done

A story is done when all of these hold. There is no partial done.

* ☐ Every acceptance criterion passes an automated test
* ☐ Unit tests for new logic; integration test for anything crossing a service or interface boundary
* ☐ Every NFR in section 20 satisfied — this is a checklist, not an aspiration
* ☐ Audit events emitted for every PHI read and write the story introduces
* ☐ Access control applied and tested with a user who should be denied
* ☐ No PHI in logs, URLs, error messages or analytics — verified, not assumed
* ☐ Error and empty states designed and implemented, not left as a blank screen
* ☐ Works at the target viewport for its persona's device
* ☐ Keyboard accessible with visible focus
* ☐ Code reviewed by someone who did not write it
* ☐ Deployed to staging and exercised by a non-author against the acceptance criteria
* ☐ Requirements document updated if the build revealed the requirement was wrong

That last item matters. The requirements document is a living artifact; a story that contradicts it means one of them is wrong, and the discrepancy gets resolved rather than silently ignored.

### Definition of Done — additional, for clinical stories

Any story touching clinical documentation, medication, specimens, dosing, intervals or codes also requires:

* ☐ Reviewed by Dr. R or a clinician before merge
* ☐ The failure mode written down: what happens if this is wrong, and who notices
* ☐ Where an agent is involved, abstention behaviour tested with deliberately degraded input

### Testing policy

Unit tests for business rules — the multiple-endoscopy sequencer, the surveillance interval table, the readiness calculator. These are pure functions with known inputs and outputs and should be tested exhaustively, including the edge cases.

Integration tests against recorded payer responses, recorded HL7 messages and sample documents. Build a fixture library early; it is the thing that lets you change the parser without fear.

End-to-end tests for the three journeys in section 2. If those three pass, the system works.

No test may use real patient data, ever, including in staging.

## 5. System context

![system context · 12 modules, 7 external systems](data:image/png;base64,)

system context · 12 modules, 7 external systems

The tinted box is the whole deliverable. Everything outside it is a contract with someone else's system, and each of those has a lead time measured in weeks (REQ-19).

Three things to take from the picture. Staff, patients and referring practices all enter through the same system — there is no separate office EHR behind it. Every external integration touches exactly one module, so a failing interface degrades one capability rather than the whole center. And the agent layer spans the modules rather than sitting beside them, which is why EP-M ships per-epic rather than as its own phase.

## 6. Case lifecycle

![case stage machine · 10 stages, 2 hard gates, 2 exits](data:image/png;base64,)

case stage machine · 10 stages, 2 hard gates, 2 exits

Stage moves forward only. A reversal — a patient sent back from the room to pre-op — is an explicit, logged transition, not an undo.

Readiness (REQ-5) runs alongside this and is recomputed on every change to the case. It blocks at the two gates and nowhere else. A case can sit at confirmed with a failed coverage check all week; it cannot pass Gate 1 without consent.

Every transition writes actor and timestamp. Those timestamps are the only source for on-time starts, turnover, PACU length of stay and withdrawal time, so treat the write path as load-bearing rather than as telemetry.

## 7. EP-A — Foundation

REQ-3, REQ-4, REQ-20. Nine stories. Nothing else can start until these are done, and they are the stories most likely to be skipped because they produce nothing a user can see.

### US-A-01 — Facility configuration (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want to record the facility's identifiers and operating parameters so that every downstream claim, report and schedule carries correct facility data.

* **AC-A-01-1** — Given no facility exists, When the administrator saves name, address, NPI, tax ID, CMS certification number, state licence with expiry, accreditor, time zone and operating hours, Then the facility is created and marked as the active facility.
* **AC-A-01-2** — Given a facility exists, When any field changes, Then the previous value is retained with its effective date range and visible in a history view.
* **AC-A-01-3** — Given a state licence expiry within 90 days, When the administrator opens the dashboard, Then a renewal warning is shown.
* **AC-A-01-4** — Given a non-administrator, When they attempt to edit facility configuration, Then the request is denied and the attempt is logged.

### US-A-02 — Rooms and bays (Must, 2)

As an administrator I want to define procedure rooms, pre-op bays and PACU bays so that scheduling can model real capacity.

* **AC-A-02-1** — Given the facility exists, When a location is created with a name, type and capacity, Then it is available for assignment.
* **AC-A-02-2** — Given a location holds future scheduled cases, When deactivation is attempted, Then it is refused and the affected cases are listed.

### US-A-03 — Providers and privileges (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want to record providers and the procedures they are privileged for so that a case cannot be booked with an unprivileged physician.

* **AC-A-03-1** — Given a provider with NPI, specialty and credentials, When privileges are granted for named procedure types with a date range, Then those procedures become bookable for that provider.
* **AC-A-03-2** — Given a provider whose privileges lapse before a scheduled case date, When the case is booked, Then booking is refused with the reason.
* **AC-A-03-3** — Given any credential expiring within 90, 60 or 30 days, When that threshold is crossed, Then the administrator is notified once per threshold.
* **AC-A-03-4** — Given a provider with a lapsed licence, When they attempt to sign documentation, Then signing is refused.

### US-A-04 — Procedure catalog (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want a curated procedure catalog so that scheduling, preference cards and coding share one definition of each procedure.

* **AC-A-04-1** — Given a catalog entry, When saved with internal name, synonyms, default CPT codes, room duration, physician duration, turnover, required equipment, preference card, specimen likelihood and anaesthesia type, Then it becomes bookable.
* **AC-A-04-2** — Given a catalog entry used by scheduled cases, When its default duration changes, Then existing scheduled cases retain the duration they were booked with.
* **AC-A-04-3** — Given a search by synonym, When a scheduler types "scope", Then matching entries are returned.

### US-A-05 — Payer configuration and auth matrix (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want payer records with an authorization requirement matrix so that clearance knows what each payer needs.

* **AC-A-05-1** — Given a payer, When saved with payer ID, clearinghouse identifier, plan types, timely filing limit and authorization channel, Then it is selectable on a coverage record.
* **AC-A-05-2** — Given a payer and a procedure type, When an authorization requirement is set, Then clearance reads it when determining whether auth is needed.
* **AC-A-05-3** — Given an authorization denial pattern on a payer and procedure, When three denials occur in 90 days, Then the administrator is alerted that the matrix may be wrong.

### US-A-06 — Preference cards (Should, 3)

As a materials manager I want versioned preference cards per physician and procedure so that the right items are picked and usage is captured accurately.

* **AC-A-06-1** — Given a physician and procedure, When a card is saved with its item list, Then it becomes the default pick list for that combination.
* **AC-A-06-2** — Given a card used on a completed case, When the card is edited, Then the completed case still shows the version that was used.

### US-A-07 — Users, roles and access policy (Must, 8)

As an administrator I want role-based access scoped to the facility so that each user sees only what their role permits.

* **AC-A-07-1** — Given the role matrix in REQ-3, When a user holds a role, Then their permitted actions match that row exactly and no other.
* **AC-A-07-2** — Given a user with multiple roles, When permissions are evaluated, Then they are the union of their roles.
* **AC-A-07-3** — Given a user with no role at a facility, When they request any record belonging to it, Then the response is identical to that for a non-existent record.
* **AC-A-07-4** — Given any role including administrator, When an attempt is made to sign or approve codes on a physician's behalf, Then it is refused.
* **AC-A-07-5** — Given a clinical workstation, When 15 minutes pass without activity, Then the session terminates and full authentication is required.

### US-A-08 — Break-glass access (Must, 3)

As any clinical user I want to read a record outside my scope in an emergency so that care is never blocked by permissions.

* **AC-A-08-1** — Given a user without scope, When they elevate and state a reason, Then read access is granted for the remainder of the shift.
* **AC-A-08-2** — Given an elevation occurred, When the administrator opens the daily report, Then every elevation appears with user, record, reason and timestamp.
* **AC-A-08-3** — Given an elevation, When the user attempts to write, Then the write is refused — break-glass is read-only.

### US-A-09 — Audit log (Must, 8)

As an administrator I want every access to PHI recorded so that I can answer an access request and satisfy a HIPAA audit.

* **AC-A-09-1** — Given any read or write of PHI by a human or an agent, When it occurs, Then an audit event records actor, actor type, record, action, timestamp and source address.
* **AC-A-09-2** — Given an agent action, When the audit event is written, Then it also records the agent name, model version and prompt version.
* **AC-A-09-3** — Given any user including administrator, When they attempt to alter or delete an audit event, Then it is refused.
* **AC-A-09-4** — Given a patient, When an access report is requested, Then every access to that patient's record is returned with the fields above.
* **AC-A-09-5** — Given an audit event, When it is six years old, Then it is still retrievable.

## 8. EP-B — Referral intake and registration

REQ-6. Eleven stories. This is the front of the funnel; a leak here is lost revenue nobody can see.

![referral intake data flow · 4 steps, 3 human queues](data:image/png;base64,)

referral intake data flow · 4 steps, 3 human queues

### US-B-01 — Receive inbound fax (Must, 5)

As the system I want every inbound fax captured as an incoming item so that nothing arrives without a record.

* **AC-B-01-1** — Given a fax arrives at the eFax provider, When the webhook fires, Then an incoming item is created with the document, channel, received timestamp and page count, within 60 seconds.
* **AC-B-01-2** — Given the webhook fails, When it is retried, Then no duplicate incoming item is created for the same provider message ID.
* **AC-B-01-3** — Given the eFax provider is unreachable for more than 15 minutes, When the gap is detected, Then the administrator is alerted.

### US-B-02 — Classify an incoming item (Must, 5)

As the system I want each item classified so that it routes to the right workflow.

* **AC-B-02-1** — Given an incoming item, When classification runs, Then it is assigned one of referral, insurance card, pathology result, prior records, correspondence or unknown, with a confidence score.
* **AC-B-02-2** — Given confidence below the configured threshold, When classification completes, Then the kind is set to unknown and a work item is created for the intake role.
* **AC-B-02-3** — Given any classification outcome, When it completes, Then the item still exists and is retrievable — no item is ever deleted by classification.

### US-B-03 — Extract referral fields (Must, 8)

As an intake nurse I want fields extracted from a referral so that I review rather than retype.

* **AC-B-03-1** — Given a referral document, When extraction runs, Then patient name, DOB, sex, address, phone, payer, member ID, group, referring provider, referring practice, requested procedure and indication are extracted, each with a confidence score.
* **AC-B-03-2** — Given any extracted field, When a reviewer clicks it, Then the source page and the region it came from are shown.
* **AC-B-03-3** — Given a field the model is not confident about, When extraction completes, Then the field is empty and flagged, never populated with a guess.
* **AC-B-03-4** — Given anticoagulant medications are named in the document, When extraction runs, Then they are captured and surfaced on the referral.

### US-B-04 — Flag urgent indications (Must, 3)

As a physician I want urgent referrals surfaced immediately so that a bleed does not sit in a queue overnight.

* **AC-B-04-1** — Given a referral whose indication matches the configured urgent list, When extraction completes, Then a high-priority work item is created and the physician notified within one hour of receipt.
* **AC-B-04-2** — Given an urgent referral unacknowledged after two hours, When the timer expires, Then the administrator is also notified.

### US-B-05 — Match to an existing patient (Must, 8)

As an intake nurse I want candidate matches presented so that I never create a duplicate.

* **AC-B-05-1** — Given normalized last name, first name and DOB all agree with exactly one patient, When matching runs, Then the referral is auto-linked.
* **AC-B-05-2** — Given last name and DOB agree but first name is a variant, When matching runs, Then both records are presented side by side for a human decision.
* **AC-B-05-3** — Given no candidate reaches the probable threshold, When matching completes, Then no patient is created and a work item asks a human to confirm a new patient.
* **AC-B-05-4** — Given any matching outcome, When it completes, Then no patient record has been created or merged without a human action.

### US-B-06 — Register a new patient (Must, 5)

As front desk I want to register a patient so that a case can be scheduled against a complete record.

* **AC-B-06-1** — Given a confirmed new patient, When legal name, DOB, sex, address, phone, preferred contact, language, emergency contact and responsible party are saved, Then the patient record is created.
* **AC-B-06-2** — Given an insurance card image, When uploaded front and back, Then it attaches to the coverage record.
* **AC-B-06-3** — Given a mobile number, When saved, Then it is flagged as SMS-capable or not.

### US-B-07 — Duplicate detection report (Should, 3)

As an administrator I want possible duplicates surfaced weekly so that the record stays clean.

* **AC-B-07-1** — Given two patients sharing DOB and a close name, When the weekly report runs, Then the pair appears with the fields that differ.
* **AC-B-07-2** — Given a confirmed duplicate, When merged, Then both records' history is preserved and the merge is reversible for 30 days.

### US-B-08 — Triage a referral (Must, 3)

As an intake nurse I want to record a triage decision so that scheduling only sees accepted referrals.

* **AC-B-08-1** — Given a reviewed referral, When a decision of accept, accept pending records, redirect to office or decline is recorded with a reason, Then the decision, actor and timestamp are stored.
* **AC-B-08-2** — Given a decision of accept, When saved, Then a case is created at stage requested.
* **AC-B-08-3** — Given a decision of decline, When saved, Then a reply is queued to the referring practice stating the reason.

### US-B-09 — Review and correct extracted fields (Must, 5)

As an intake nurse I want to correct extraction before anything downstream uses it so that errors do not propagate.

* **AC-B-09-1** — Given extracted fields, When a reviewer edits any value, Then the original extracted value is retained alongside the correction.
* **AC-B-09-2** — Given corrections exist, When a case is created, Then the corrected values are used.

### US-B-10 — Capture a phone referral (Should, 2)

As front desk I want to key a referral taken by phone so that the same downstream flow applies.

* **AC-B-10-1** — Given a manual intake form, When submitted, Then a referral is created identical in structure to an extracted one, with channel set to phone.

### US-B-11 — Intake worklist (Must, 3)

As an intake nurse I want one queue showing everything waiting on me so that nothing is missed.

* **AC-B-11-1** — Given open work items for the intake role, When the worklist loads, Then they are shown sorted by priority then age.
* **AC-B-11-2** — Given an item older than its configured threshold, When the worklist loads, Then it is visually distinguished as overdue.

## 9. EP-C — Scheduling and block management

REQ-7. Ten stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open question 3** (parallel office clinic) — US-C-10 cannot be specified until that is answered.

### US-C-01 — Define block time (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want recurring blocks per physician and room so that capacity is allocated before it is booked.

* **AC-C-01-1** — Given a room and a physician, When a block is saved with a day pattern, start, end and effective date range, Then it appears on the schedule for every matching date in range.
* **AC-C-01-2** — Given a block with scheduled cases, When its times are narrowed, Then cases now outside it are listed and the change requires confirmation.
* **AC-C-01-3** — Given overlapping blocks for the same room, When saving, Then the save is refused.

### US-C-02 — Book a case (Must, 8)

As a scheduler I want to book a case into a block so that the patient has a date, room and physician.

* **AC-C-02-1** — Given an accepted referral, When a procedure, physician, room, date and time are selected, Then a case is created at stage scheduled with its duration taken from the catalog.
* **AC-C-02-2** — Given a physician not privileged for the selected procedure, When booking is attempted, Then it is refused naming the missing privilege.
* **AC-C-02-3** — Given a room not equipped for the procedure, When booking is attempted, Then it is refused.
* **AC-C-02-4** — Given the required scope is already committed at that time, When booking is attempted, Then a warning is shown and booking proceeds only on acknowledgement.
* **AC-C-02-5** — Given the duration exceeds remaining block time, When booking is attempted, Then a warning is shown with the overrun in minutes.
* **AC-C-02-6** — Given a case is booked, When it is saved, Then the pre-op timeline work items in US-E-01 are generated.

### US-C-03 — ASC appropriateness screen (Must, 5)

As an anaesthesia provider I want high-risk patients flagged at booking so that they are reviewed before the day.

* **AC-C-03-1** — Given a patient matching any configured trigger (ASA IV or above, BMI above threshold, severe OSA, unstable cardiac history, dialysis dependence, age above limit), When a case is booked, Then the case is flagged for anaesthesia review and cannot reach stage confirmed until reviewed.
* **AC-C-03-2** — Given a flagged case, When anaesthesia records a review outcome with a reason, Then the case may be confirmed, redirected to hospital outpatient, or cancelled.
* **AC-C-03-3** — Given triggers are configuration, When an administrator changes a threshold, Then already-reviewed cases are not re-flagged.

### US-C-04 — Reschedule a case (Must, 5)

As a scheduler I want to move a case so that downstream state follows the new date.

* **AC-C-04-1** — Given a scheduled case, When the date or time changes, Then every pre-op timeline work item recomputes against the new date.
* **AC-C-04-2** — Given the case has an approved authorization, When the date moves outside the authorization's valid range, Then the authorization check moves to failed, readiness becomes blocked, and a revalidation work item is created.
* **AC-C-04-3** — Given prep instructions were already sent, When the case moves, Then reissued instructions are queued with the new second-dose timing.
* **AC-C-04-4** — Given an eligibility response older than 30 days from the new date, When the case moves, Then the coverage check moves to pending.

### US-C-05 — Cancel a case (Must, 3)

As any staff member I want to cancel with a structured reason so that cancellation patterns are measurable.

* **AC-C-05-1** — Given a case at any stage before procedure\_start, When cancelled, Then a reason from the controlled list is required and the stage becomes cancelled.
* **AC-C-05-2** — Given a cancellation, When it is saved, Then actor, timestamp, reason and the stage it was cancelled from are recorded.
* **AC-C-05-3** — Given a cancellation inside 24 hours, When saved, Then the slot is offered to the short-notice waitlist.

### US-C-06 — Block release (Should, 3)

As an administrator I want unused block time released automatically so that other physicians can use it.

* **AC-C-06-1** — Given unbooked block time at the configured horizon, When the horizon passes, Then that time moves to the open pool and the block owner is notified.
* **AC-C-06-2** — Given released time, When another physician books into it, Then the booking succeeds without administrator intervention.

### US-C-07 — Short-notice waitlist (Should, 5)

As a scheduler I want a waitlist so that same-day gaps get filled.

* **AC-C-07-1** — Given a patient who consented to short notice, When a slot opens, Then candidates are ranked by clinical urgency then by wait time.
* **AC-C-07-2** — Given a candidate is contacted and accepts, When confirmed, Then the case is booked and the patient's original date released.
* **AC-C-07-3** — Given a candidate whose prep could not be completed in time, When ranking runs, Then they are excluded.

### US-C-08 — Learned duration (Could, 3)

As a scheduler I want to see a physician's actual average duration so that the day schedules realistically.

* **AC-C-08-1** — Given at least 20 completed cases of a procedure by a physician, When booking that combination, Then both the catalog default and the observed mean are shown.
* **AC-C-08-2** — Given the observed mean is shown, When the scheduler accepts the default, Then nothing is auto-adjusted.

### US-C-09 — Day view (Must, 5)

As a physician I want today's list with readiness per case so that I know what needs me before I start.

* **AC-C-09-1** — Given cases scheduled today, When the day view loads, Then each shows time, patient, procedure and exactly one readiness state.
* **AC-C-09-2** — Given a case with a failed readiness check, When displayed, Then the specific failing check is named, not merely a colour.
* **AC-C-09-3** — Given the view loads with a full day, When measured, Then it renders within 1 second at p95.

### US-C-10 — Patient self-scheduling (Won't, phase 2)

Deferred. Depends on REQ-22 open question 3.

## 10. EP-D — Financial clearance

REQ-8. Twelve stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open question 6** (clearinghouse) — nothing in this epic can be integration-tested until that is chosen.

![financial clearance pipeline · 10 steps, 1 bypass](data:image/png;base64,)

financial clearance pipeline · 10 steps, 1 bypass

Two exception paths are not drawn: an incomplete 271 routes to human verification rather than forward, and a denial routes to an appeal work item. Both are specified below.

### US-D-01 — Run eligibility (Must, 8)

As the system I want to verify coverage automatically so that staff never key a payer portal.

* **AC-D-01-1** — Given a case with a coverage record, When it is booked, at 7 days before, and at 06:00 on the procedure date, Then a 270 is submitted and the 271 parsed.
* **AC-D-01-2** — Given a 271 response, When parsed, Then active status, plan name and type, effective and termination dates, subscriber relationship and network status are stored.
* **AC-D-01-3** — Given any 271, When stored, Then the raw response is retained unmodified and retrievable.
* **AC-D-01-4** — Given a 271 returning coverage terminated before the procedure date, When parsed, Then the coverage check moves to failed and a work item is created.

### US-D-02 — Handle a degraded eligibility response (Must, 5)

As a financial clearance specialist I want incomplete payer responses treated as unknown so that we never assume coverage that does not exist.

* **AC-D-02-1** — Given a 271 that is silent on the requested service type, When parsed, Then the result is recorded as response incomplete, not as covered.
* **AC-D-02-2** — Given a result of response incomplete, When readiness is computed, Then the coverage check is pending and a verification work item exists.
* **AC-D-02-3** — Given a result of response incomplete, When any screen displays coverage, Then it is never rendered as confirmed coverage.
* **AC-D-02-4** — Given a payer returns only plan-level benefits, When parsed, Then the same treatment applies.

### US-D-03 — Capture benefits (Must, 5)

As a financial clearance specialist I want the patient's benefit position so that an accurate estimate can be produced.

* **AC-D-03-1** — Given a usable 271, When benefits are parsed, Then individual and family deductible and remaining, coinsurance, copay, out-of-pocket maximum and remaining, and the ASC facility benefit are stored.
* **AC-D-03-2** — Given a screening procedure and a plan with a preventive benefit, When benefits are parsed, Then the screening benefit applicability is recorded as a distinct field.

### US-D-04 — Determine authorization requirement (Must, 3)

As the system I want to know whether auth is needed so that cases are not submitted unnecessarily or missed.

* **AC-D-04-1** — Given a payer, plan and procedure, When clearance runs, Then the auth matrix is consulted and the authorization state set to required or not\_required.
* **AC-D-04-2** — Given no matrix entry exists for that combination, When clearance runs, Then the state is required and a work item asks a human to confirm — the safe default is to assume auth is needed.
* **AC-D-04-3** — Given a determination, When made, Then the matrix rule that produced it is recorded on the case.

### US-D-05 — Assemble the authorization packet (Must, 5)

As a financial clearance specialist I want the clinical packet assembled so that I do not gather documents by hand.

* **AC-D-05-1** — Given a case needing auth, When assembly runs, Then the referral, documented indication, relevant history, prior endoscopy and prior pathology are collected into a packet.
* **AC-D-05-2** — Given a required document is missing, When assembly runs, Then the packet is not submitted and a work item names the missing item.

### US-D-06 — Submit and track authorization (Must, 8)

As a financial clearance specialist I want submission and follow-up handled so that nothing sits unanswered.

* **AC-D-06-1** — Given a complete packet and a payer supporting 278, When submission runs, Then a 278 is sent and the response recorded.
* **AC-D-06-2** — Given a payer without 278, When submission runs, Then the configured channel is used and the submission logged with evidence.
* **AC-D-06-3** — Given a submitted authorization with no response after the payer's configured turnaround, When the timer expires, Then a follow-up work item is created.
* **AC-D-06-4** — Given an approval, When recorded, Then the authorization number, valid date range and approved units are stored and the authorization check becomes satisfied.
* **AC-D-06-5** — Given a denial, When received, Then the authorization state becomes denied, a work item is created, and no automated acceptance of the denial occurs.

### US-D-07 — Revalidate authorization on reschedule (Must, 3)

See US-C-04 AC-C-04-2. Listed here for traceability; implemented once.

* **AC-D-07-1** — Given an approved authorization, When the procedure date moves outside its valid range, Then the check fails and readiness blocks.
* **AC-D-07-2** — Given an authorization within 7 days of expiry and a case still scheduled after it, When the daily sweep runs, Then a work item is created.

### US-D-08 — Flag procedure divergence from authorization (Should, 3)

As a coder I want to know when the procedure performed differs from the one authorized so that I can act before the claim goes out.

* **AC-D-08-1** — Given an authorization for a named procedure, When coding is finalized for a different procedure, Then a flag is raised on the case before claim build.

### US-D-09 — Produce the patient estimate (Must, 5)

As a patient I want to know what I will owe so that I am not surprised by a bill.

* **AC-D-09-1** — Given benefits and an expected allowed amount, When the estimate is generated, Then it states the expected patient responsibility.
* **AC-D-09-2** — Given a screening colonoscopy, When the estimate is generated, Then it states both the screening outcome and the outcome if the procedure becomes therapeutic.
* **AC-D-09-3** — Given an estimate, When it is delivered at least 3 days before the procedure through the patient's preferred channel, Then delivery and any acknowledgement are recorded.
* **AC-D-09-4** — Given an uninsured or self-pay patient, When a case is booked, Then a good-faith estimate is generated.

### US-D-10 — Collect the patient portion (Must, 5)

As front desk I want to take payment so that the balance is settled before service.

* **AC-D-10-1** — Given an estimate, When payment is taken by card, Then it posts to the case and the receipt is issued.
* **AC-D-10-2** — Given a patient who cannot pay in full, When a payment plan is created, Then the schedule is recorded and the estimate check is satisfied.
* **AC-D-10-3** — Given any write-off or discount, When applied, Then it requires a human with the financial role and records actor and reason.

### US-D-11 — Clearance worklist (Must, 3)

As a financial clearance specialist I want one prioritized queue so that I work the right case next.

* **AC-D-11-1** — Given open clearance work items, When the worklist loads, Then they are sorted by procedure date then priority.
* **AC-D-11-2** — Given a case whose procedure date is within 48 hours and whose readiness is blocked, When the worklist loads, Then it appears at the top regardless of other sorting.

### US-D-12 — Readiness recomputation (Must, 5)

As the system I want readiness recomputed on every relevant change so that the displayed state is never stale.

* **AC-D-12-1** — Given any change to coverage, benefits, authorization, consent, H&P, anticoagulation, anaesthesia clearance, prep, escort or equipment, When it is saved, Then readiness is recomputed within 2 seconds.
* **AC-D-12-2** — Given all checks satisfied or waived, When recomputed, Then overall readiness is ready.
* **AC-D-12-3** — Given any check failed, When recomputed, Then overall readiness is blocked and the failing checks are enumerable.
* **AC-D-12-4** — Given a waiver, When applied, Then it records actor, role, reason and timestamp; consent and identity cannot be waived by any role.

## 11. EP-E — Pre-operative readiness

REQ-9. Eleven stories. This epic prevents same-day cancellations, which are the most expensive recurring failure in an ASC.

### US-E-01 — Generate the pre-op timeline (Must, 5)

As the system I want scheduled work items generated on booking so that nothing depends on someone remembering.

* **AC-E-01-1** — Given a case is booked, When it is saved, Then work items are created for each row of the REQ-9 timeline, each dated relative to the procedure date.
* **AC-E-01-2** — Given the procedure date changes, When saved, Then every incomplete timeline item recomputes and completed ones are retained with their original completion date.
* **AC-E-01-3** — Given a timeline item whose computed date is already past at booking, When generated, Then it is created as immediately due rather than skipped.

### US-E-02 — Track H&P validity (Must, 5)

As a pre-op nurse I want H&P expiry tracked continuously so that it is never discovered on the morning.

* **AC-E-02-1** — Given an H&P with a date, When readiness is computed, Then the hp check is satisfied only if the H&P is dated within 30 days of the procedure date.
* **AC-E-02-2** — Given an H&P that will be expired by the procedure date, When the daily sweep runs 7 days out, Then a work item is created.
* **AC-E-02-3** — Given a pre-procedure update note is required, When the H&P is present but no update exists, Then the hp check remains pending.
* **AC-E-02-4** — Given the hp check is not satisfied, When Gate 1 is attempted, Then the transition is blocked pending an override.

### US-E-03 — Capture anticoagulation status (Must, 8)

As a pre-op nurse I want anticoagulation handled as a structured workflow so that a hold is never assumed.

* **AC-E-03-1** — Given any patient, When pre-op intake is completed, Then an explicit yes or no is recorded for anticoagulant or antiplatelet use — an empty field does not satisfy the check.
* **AC-E-03-2** — Given the patient takes an agent, When recorded, Then agent, dose, indication and prescribing physician are captured.
* **AC-E-03-3** — Given an agent and the procedure's bleeding risk, When the rule table is applied, Then a recommended hold window is displayed to the nurse as a suggestion with its rule version.
* **AC-E-03-4** — Given a recommendation exists, When the check is evaluated, Then it is satisfied only once the prescriber's actual instruction is recorded with the date it was given.
* **AC-E-03-5** — Given a hold instruction exists, When the day-before confirmation call completes, Then the patient's confirmation that they held it is recorded separately.
* **AC-E-03-6** — Given any patient-facing message, When generated by the system, Then it never instructs the patient to stop, start or change a medication.

### US-E-04 — Health questionnaire (Must, 5)

As a pre-op nurse I want the patient's history collected before the call so that the call is short and targeted.

* **AC-E-04-1** — Given a scheduled case, When the questionnaire is sent, Then it covers medications and supplements, allergies with reaction, prior anaesthesia problems, cardiac and pulmonary history, sleep apnoea and CPAP, diabetes regimen, pregnancy status where applicable, mobility needs, prior abdominal surgery and prior difficult endoscopy.
* **AC-E-04-2** — Given a patient who cannot complete it digitally, When the nurse opens the same form, Then it can be completed by phone with the source recorded.
* **AC-E-04-3** — Given completed responses, When the anaesthesia assessment is opened, Then the responses populate it as input and do not substitute for assessment.

### US-E-05 — Anaesthesia assessment (Must, 5)

As an anaesthesia provider I want to record the pre-anaesthesia assessment so that the case is cleared to proceed.

* **AC-E-05-1** — Given a case, When the assessment is saved with airway assessment, Mallampati, ASA class, plan, NPO instruction and precautions, Then the anesthesia\_clearance check is satisfied.
* **AC-E-05-2** — Given a case flagged by US-C-03, When no documented review exists, Then the case cannot reach confirmed.
* **AC-E-05-3** — Given the check is not satisfied, When Gate 2 is attempted, Then the transition is blocked pending an override.

### US-E-06 — Prep prescription and instructions (Must, 5)

As a patient I want prep instructions I can follow so that my examination is not wasted.

* **AC-E-06-1** — Given a booked case, When instructions are generated, Then the second-dose timing is computed from the actual arrival time, not a generic template.
* **AC-E-06-2** — Given a patient language preference, When instructions are generated, Then they are produced in that language where a translation exists, and flagged for human handling where it does not.
* **AC-E-06-3** — Given instructions were sent, When the case is rescheduled, Then revised instructions are queued with new timings.

### US-E-07 — Confirmation call (Must, 5)

As a pre-op nurse I want a structured day-before call so that every day-of blocker is caught.

* **AC-E-07-1** — Given a case one day out, When the call script is opened, Then it requires arrival time confirmation, NPO instruction, escort name and phone, anticoagulation hold confirmation and prep progress.
* **AC-E-07-2** — Given the escort fields are completed, When saved, Then the escort check is satisfied.
* **AC-E-07-3** — Given the patient reports inadequate prep progress, When recorded, Then the prep check moves to failed and a work item is created for the scheduler.
* **AC-E-07-4** — Given the call is not completed by a configured cutoff, When the cutoff passes, Then the case appears as at-risk on the next-day readiness view.

### US-E-08 — Prep quality question (Must, 2)

As a pre-op nurse I want to ask about effluent specifically so that prep failure is caught the day before.

* **AC-E-08-1** — Given the confirmation call, When prep is discussed, Then a structured answer about effluent appearance is recorded, not free text alone.

### US-E-09 — Consent capture (Must, 5)

As a pre-op nurse I want consent recorded before sedation so that the legal requirement is met.

* **AC-E-09-1** — Given a case, When consent is signed, Then it names the specific procedure and the performing physician and is stored with signature, signer and timestamp.
* **AC-E-09-2** — Given consent names a different procedure than the one scheduled, When readiness is computed, Then the consent check is failed.
* **AC-E-09-3** — Given the consent check is unsatisfied, When Gate 1 is attempted, Then the transition is blocked, and the consent check cannot be waived by any role.

### US-E-10 — Equipment reservation check (Should, 3)

As a circulator I want the required scope confirmed available so that a case is not held up at the door.

* **AC-E-10-1** — Given a case requiring a scope type, When readiness is computed, Then the equipment check is satisfied only if an instance is available, successfully reprocessed and within hang time at the scheduled time.

### US-E-11 — Next-day readiness view (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want tomorrow's list with every blocker visible so that the evening huddle is useful.

* **AC-E-11-1** — Given tomorrow's cases, When the view loads, Then each shows its readiness state and every failing or pending check by name.
* **AC-E-11-2** — Given a case whose readiness is blocked, When the view loads, Then the owning role for each failing check is shown.
* **AC-E-11-3** — Given the view, When exported, Then it produces the printed downtime pack described in REQ-21.

## 12. EP-F — Day of surgery

REQ-10. Thirteen stories. Every screen in this epic is used standing, often gloved, with a sedated patient in the room. NFR-2 (500 ms saves) is not negotiable here.

![day-of-surgery swimlane · 5 roles, 10 steps, 2 gates](data:image/png;base64,)

day-of-surgery swimlane · 5 roles, 10 steps, 2 gates

### US-F-01 — Check in a patient (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-01-1** — Given an arriving patient, When two identifiers are verified, Then the identity check is satisfied and the stage becomes arrived.
* **AC-F-01-2** — Given demographics or insurance have changed, When updated at check-in, Then eligibility re-runs immediately.
* **AC-F-01-3** — Given an outstanding patient balance, When check-in opens, Then the amount and payment options are shown to front desk.
* **AC-F-01-4** — Given the escort check is unsatisfied, When check-in completes, Then it is surfaced as a blocker before the patient leaves the desk.

### US-F-02 — Enforce Gate 1 (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-02-1** — Given a case at arrived, When transition to preop is attempted and identity, consent or hp is unsatisfied, Then the transition is refused and the failing checks named.
* **AC-F-02-2** — Given a refusal, When a permitted role overrides with a reason, Then the transition proceeds and actor, reason, timestamp and overridden state are recorded.
* **AC-F-02-3** — Given the consent or identity check, When an override is attempted, Then it is refused for every role including administrator.

### US-F-03 — Pre-op assessment and vitals (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-03-1** — Given a patient in a bay, When height, weight, temperature, blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate and oxygen saturation are recorded, Then they attach to the encounter with timestamp and recorder.
* **AC-F-03-2** — Given IV placement, When recorded with site and gauge, Then it is stored on the nursing record.
* **AC-F-03-3** — Given medication reconciliation is completed, When saved, Then the medication list is versioned on this encounter.
* **AC-F-03-4** — Given a work-in-progress assessment, When the nurse is interrupted and navigates away, Then no entered data is lost.

### US-F-04 — Pre-procedure H&P update (Must, 3)

* **AC-F-04-1** — Given an existing H&P, When the physician records and signs an update confirming no interval change, Then the hp check is satisfied.
* **AC-F-04-2** — Given the update, When signed, Then it is immutable and carries signer, credential and timestamp.

### US-F-05 — Timeout (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-05-1** — Given a case at preop, When the timeout is performed, Then correct patient, procedure, site and laterality, consent verified, allergies reviewed, equipment present, prophylaxis if indicated and anticipated issues are each recorded as discrete confirmations.
* **AC-F-05-2** — Given a timeout, When saved, Then every participant present is named and the timestamp recorded.
* **AC-F-05-3** — Given no completed timeout, When procedure\_start is attempted, Then it is refused.
* **AC-F-05-4** — Given a completed timeout, When retrieved for a survey, Then it is a discrete record, not a field inside the procedure note.

### US-F-06 — Enforce Gate 2 (Must, 3)

* **AC-F-06-1** — Given a case at preop, When transition to in\_room is attempted and anesthesia\_clearance, anticoagulation, equipment or escort is unsatisfied, Then the transition is refused and the failing checks named.
* **AC-F-06-2** — Given a refusal, When overridden by a permitted role with a reason, Then it is logged as in AC-F-02-2.

### US-F-07 — Intra-procedure event log (Must, 8)

* **AC-F-07-1** — Given a case in the room, When the circulator marks room-in, sedation start, scope-in, cecal intubation, scope-out and room-out, Then each is stored with its own timestamp and actor.
* **AC-F-07-2** — Given scope-out follows cecal intubation, When both exist, Then withdrawal time is computed and stored.
* **AC-F-07-3** — Given a case in progress, When the withdrawal timer is running, Then it is visible to the physician in the room and updates live.
* **AC-F-07-4** — Given the scope in use, When the case starts, Then its serial number is recorded on the case.
* **AC-F-07-5** — Given any intra-op save, When measured, Then it completes within 500 ms at p95.

### US-F-08 — Medication administration (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-08-1** — Given a medication given in the room, When recorded, Then agent, dose, route, time and administering clinician are stored.
* **AC-F-08-2** — Given a controlled substance, When recorded, Then waste and witness are captured where required.

### US-F-09 — Sedation monitoring (Should, 5)

* **AC-F-09-1** — Given a case under sedation, When vitals are recorded at the protocol interval, Then they attach to the anaesthesia record with timestamps.
* **AC-F-09-2** — Given a connected monitor, When the interface is live, Then vitals populate automatically and are marked as device-sourced.

### US-F-10 — PACU recovery (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-10-1** — Given a patient in recovery, When arrival vitals and subsequent interval vitals are recorded, Then each is timestamped and attributed.
* **AC-F-10-2** — Given the recovery score protocol, When scored at each interval, Then the score and its components are stored.
* **AC-F-10-3** — Given pain, nausea, fluid tolerance, ambulation and voiding assessments, When recorded, Then they attach to the PACU record.

### US-F-11 — Discharge criteria and discharge (Must, 5)

* **AC-F-11-1** — Given configured discharge criteria, When any is unmet, Then recording discharge is refused.
* **AC-F-11-2** — Given a physician override of an unmet criterion, When applied, Then it is logged with actor and reason.
* **AC-F-11-3** — Given discharge, When recorded, Then condition, escort identity, instructions given and who received them are stored.
* **AC-F-11-4** — Given discharge instructions, When generated, Then they include diet, activity, anticoagulation restart timing, warning signs with a contact number, and how pathology results will be communicated.

### US-F-12 — Day-of exception flows (Must, 8)

* **AC-F-12-1** — Given a case cancelled after arrival but before sedation, When recorded, Then the stage becomes cancelled, the reason is captured, and no procedure charges are generated.
* **AC-F-12-2** — Given a case aborted after sedation started, When recorded, Then the partial procedure is documented, modifier 73 or 74 handling is flagged to coding, and the case proceeds to PACU.
* **AC-F-12-3** — Given a procedure extended beyond what was consented, When documented, Then a flag is raised for coding and for QAPI review.
* **AC-F-12-4** — Given a patient transferred to hospital, When recorded, Then an incident report is opened automatically and the ASCQR transfer measure is incremented.
* **AC-F-12-5** — Given a complication requiring intervention, When documented, Then it is captured as a discrete complication record, not only as narrative.

### US-F-13 — Patient self check-in (Should, 5)

* **AC-F-13-1** — Given a patient with a case today, When they open self check-in, Then they can confirm demographics, complete questionnaires and pay without creating an account.
* **AC-F-13-2** — Given self check-in is completed, When the patient arrives, Then front desk performs only identity verification and escort confirmation.
* **AC-F-13-3** — Given identity verification, When attempted through self check-in, Then it is refused — a human must perform it.

## 13. EP-G — Clinical documentation

REQ-11. Ten stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open question 8** (transcript retention) for US-G-05 onward.

### US-G-01 — Structured findings (Must, 8)

As a physician I want findings recorded as discrete objects so that coding, pathology and surveillance can read them.

* **AC-G-01-1** — Given a procedure, When a finding is recorded, Then anatomical location, size in mm, morphology using Paris classification, action taken and whether a specimen was retrieved are stored as separate fields.
* **AC-G-01-2** — Given a finding with an intervention, When saved, Then the technique is recorded from a controlled list — cold snare, hot snare, EMR, biopsy, clip, injection, APC, dilation with size.
* **AC-G-01-3** — Given a size is not known, When the finding is saved, Then the field is empty and flagged, never defaulted.
* **AC-G-01-4** — Given findings exist, When coding runs, Then it reads the structured findings and not the narrative.

### US-G-02 — Procedure note (Must, 8)

As a physician I want a complete note so that the record is legally sufficient and the referrer is informed.

* **AC-G-02-1** — Given a completed procedure, When the note is assembled, Then every element in the REQ-11 table is present or explicitly marked absent.
* **AC-G-02-2** — Given a colonoscopy, When the note is assembled, Then Boston Bowel Prep Scale per segment, extent reached, and withdrawal time are present.
* **AC-G-02-3** — Given complications, When none occurred, Then the note states so explicitly rather than omitting the field.
* **AC-G-02-4** — Given a note is not signed, When discharge is attempted, Then either the note is signed or an immediate post-procedure note documenting findings, specimens and complications exists.

### US-G-03 — Signature and immutability (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want signed documents frozen so that the record withstands audit.

* **AC-G-03-1** — Given a document is signed, When saved, Then signer identity, credential and timestamp are stored and the content becomes immutable.
* **AC-G-03-2** — Given a signed document, When a change is needed, Then an addendum is created that references the original, carries its own signature, and leaves the original text visible.
* **AC-G-03-3** — Given any role including administrator, When direct edit of signed content is attempted, Then it is refused.

### US-G-04 — Photo capture and landmarks (Should, 5)

As a physician I want landmark images labelled so that completeness of the examination is evidenced.

* **AC-G-04-1** — Given images captured during a case, When attached, Then each can be labelled and associated with a specific finding.
* **AC-G-04-2** — Given a colonoscopy, When landmark images for cecum, appendiceal orifice, ileocecal valve and rectal retroflexion are attached, Then each is explicitly labelled as that landmark.
* **AC-G-04-3** — Given a complete examination is claimed, When no labelled landmark image exists, Then the note flags it for the physician before signing.

### US-G-05 — Ambient capture (Should, 13 — split before sprint)

As a physician I want the system to listen and draft so that I do not type after every case.

* **AC-G-05-1** — Given a case in the room, When capture is active, Then it is clearly indicated in the room and recorded on the case.
* **AC-G-05-2** — Given a transcript and the circulator's logged events, When the draft is produced, Then logged timestamps and specimen labels take precedence over the transcript.
* **AC-G-05-3** — Given a drafted element, When the physician inspects it, Then the source utterance or logged event that produced it is shown.
* **AC-G-05-4** — Given a clinically material value the model is uncertain about — a size, a location, whether a specimen was retrieved — When drafting, Then the field is left empty and flagged.
* **AC-G-05-5** — Given a draft, When produced, Then its state is draft and no configuration permits auto-signing.
* **AC-G-05-6** — Given the case ends, When the draft is produced, Then it is available within 2 minutes.

### US-G-06 — Review and sign the drafted note (Must, 5)

As a physician I want review to make disagreement as cheap as agreement so that I actually read it.

* **AC-G-06-1** — Given a draft, When review opens, Then flagged and uncertain fields are surfaced first.
* **AC-G-06-2** — Given the physician edits a drafted value, When saved, Then both the drafted value and the correction are retained.
* **AC-G-06-3** — Given a draft with any unresolved flagged field, When signing is attempted, Then the physician is required to resolve or explicitly accept each one.

### US-G-07 — Nursing documentation (Must, 5)

* **AC-G-07-1** — Given pre-op, intra-op, PACU and discharge records, When each is completed, Then each is a separate signed document with its own author and timestamp.
* **AC-G-07-2** — Given a nursing record, When a physician views the chart, Then it is visible but not editable by them.

### US-G-08 — Anaesthesia record (Must, 5)

* **AC-G-08-1** — Given a case, When the anaesthesia provider completes the pre-anaesthesia assessment, intra-procedure record and post-anaesthesia evaluation, Then each is signed separately.
* **AC-G-08-2** — Given the intra-procedure record, When saved, Then it contains vitals at the monitoring interval and every medication administered.

### US-G-09 — Referring provider letter (Should, 3)

As a referring physician I want the result promptly so that I keep sending patients here.

* **AC-G-09-1** — Given a signed procedure note, When it is signed, Then a letter to the referring practice is queued through their configured channel.
* **AC-G-09-2** — Given pathology returns later, When the result is acknowledged, Then a follow-up letter is queued.

### US-G-10 — Chart view (Must, 5)

As a physician I want the patient's history in one place so that I can make interval decisions.

* **AC-G-10-1** — Given a patient with prior cases, When the chart loads, Then prior procedures, findings, pathology results and surveillance intervals are shown in date order.
* **AC-G-10-2** — Given the chart loads, When measured, Then it renders within 1 second at p95.

## 14. EP-H — Specimens and pathology

REQ-12. Nine stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open questions 5 and 7** (lab choice, result-communication policy). This is the epic where a defect becomes a patient harm event rather than an inconvenience.

![specimen closed loop · 10 steps, 1 recall cycle](data:image/png;base64,)

specimen closed loop · 10 steps, 1 recall cycle

### US-H-01 — Capture a specimen (Must, 5)

* **AC-H-01-1** — Given a finding producing tissue, When a specimen is recorded, Then container label, source finding, anatomical site, fragment count, fixative and collection timestamp are stored.
* **AC-H-01-2** — Given a specimen is recorded, When the label is printed, Then it carries patient identifiers, the label letter, the site and the collection time.
* **AC-H-01-3** — Given labels are assigned, When a second specimen is recorded, Then it receives the next letter in sequence automatically.

### US-H-02 — Reconcile specimen count (Must, 3)

* **AC-H-02-1** — Given a case with specimens, When case closure is attempted, Then the count recorded on the note must equal the number of containers logged.
* **AC-H-02-2** — Given a mismatch, When closure is attempted, Then it is refused and the discrepancy is shown.

### US-H-03 — Generate the requisition (Must, 5)

* **AC-H-03-1** — Given a case with specimens, When the requisition is generated, Then it contains demographics, ordering physician, clinical history, indication, each specimen with site and finding description, and the relevant ICD-10 codes.
* **AC-H-03-2** — Given a lab with an electronic interface, When the requisition is complete, Then it transmits as HL7 ORM; otherwise it prints.

### US-H-04 — Chain of custody (Must, 5)

* **AC-H-04-1** — Given a specimen, When each handoff occurs — collected, received by processing, on the courier manifest, picked up, received by the lab — Then each is recorded with timestamp and person.
* **AC-H-04-2** — Given no lab receipt confirmation within the configured window, When the sweep runs, Then an alert is raised.

### US-H-05 — Receive and match a result (Must, 8)

* **AC-H-05-1** — Given an inbound HL7 ORU, When parsed, Then it is matched to a case and to a specific specimen by container label.
* **AC-H-05-2** — Given a result that cannot be matched with confidence, When processed, Then it goes to a human queue immediately and is never filed silently.
* **AC-H-05-3** — Given a result arrives as PDF, When processed, Then the same matching and queueing rules apply.
* **AC-H-05-4** — Given a matched result, When stored, Then it attaches to the specimen, the finding and the case.

### US-H-06 — Open-specimen register (Must, 5)

* **AC-H-06-1** — Given every specimen sent, When the register is queried, Then each shows whether a result has been received.
* **AC-H-06-2** — Given a specimen outstanding past the configured turnaround, When the daily sweep runs, Then the physician and administrator are notified.
* **AC-H-06-3** — Given any specimen in the last two years, When the exception report runs, Then it shows collection, lab receipt, result, physician acknowledgement, patient notification and interval set — and names any step not completed.

### US-H-07 — Physician acknowledgement (Must, 3)

* **AC-H-07-1** — Given a result, When the physician acknowledges it, Then an explicit action with timestamp is recorded — opening the chart does not count.
* **AC-H-07-2** — Given a result unacknowledged past the configured window, When the sweep runs, Then it escalates.

### US-H-08 — Critical result routing (Must, 5)

* **AC-H-08-1** — Given a result containing malignancy, high-grade dysplasia or any configured critical finding, When received, Then it is flagged and routed to the physician within one hour.
* **AC-H-08-2** — Given a critical result unacknowledged after the configured interval, When the timer expires, Then it escalates to the administrator.
* **AC-H-08-3** — Given a critical result, When patient notification is planned, Then a clinician phone call is required and no automated message is sent in its place.

### US-H-09 — Patient result notification (Must, 5)

* **AC-H-09-1** — Given an acknowledged result, When the patient is notified, Then channel, date, who notified and what was communicated are recorded.
* **AC-H-09-2** — Given a normal result, When notification is due, Then the configured normal-result channel and window apply.
* **AC-H-09-3** — Given an outstanding notification past its window, When the sweep runs, Then it remains an open work item and escalates.

## 15. EP-I — Inventory, scopes and reprocessing

REQ-13. Eight stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open question 10** (boundary with the procurement app) — resolve before US-I-01.

### US-I-01 — Item master (Must, 3)

* **AC-I-01-1** — Given an item, When saved with description, manufacturer, catalog number, unit of measure, vendor, cost, billable flag, par level, reorder point and storage location, Then it is available for usage capture.
* **AC-I-01-2** — Given an item marked lot-tracked or serial-tracked, When received, Then lot or serial and expiry are required.

### US-I-02 — Capture usage from a preference card (Must, 5)

* **AC-I-02-1** — Given a case with a preference card, When the circulator opens usage capture, Then the card's items are pre-filled as presumed used.
* **AC-I-02-2** — Given pre-filled items, When the circulator confirms or adjusts and saves, Then inventory decrements and the usage attaches to the case.
* **AC-I-02-3** — Given usage capture, When measured in-room, Then saves complete within 500 ms at p95.

### US-I-03 — Scan high-value and tracked items (Must, 3)

* **AC-I-03-1** — Given a lot-tracked, high-cost or implantable item, When used, Then it must be scanned and is never presumed from the preference card.
* **AC-I-03-2** — Given a scanned item, When recorded, Then lot, serial and expiry attach to the case.

### US-I-04 — Scope register (Must, 5)

* **AC-I-04-1** — Given a scope, When registered with model, serial number and purchase date, Then it is trackable individually.
* **AC-I-04-2** — Given a scope, When its state changes between available, in use, in reprocessing, in repair and quarantined, Then the change is timestamped.
* **AC-I-04-3** — Given a case, When it starts, Then the scope serial in use is recorded on the case.
* **AC-I-04-4** — Given a scope serial and a date range, When queried, Then every patient scoped with it in that range is returned.

### US-I-05 — Reprocessing record (Must, 5)

* **AC-I-05-1** — Given a reprocessing cycle, When completed, Then scope serial, cycle identifier, reprocessor machine, operator, start and end time, chemical lot, leak test result and outcome are recorded.
* **AC-I-05-2** — Given a scope whose most recent cycle did not complete successfully, When assignment to a case is attempted, Then it is refused.
* **AC-I-05-3** — Given a scope outside its hang-time limit, When assignment is attempted, Then it is refused.
* **AC-I-05-4** — Given a refusal under AC-I-05-2 or AC-I-05-3, When an override is attempted, Then it is refused for every role — this gate has no override.

### US-I-06 — Par levels and reordering (Should, 3)

* **AC-I-06-1** — Given stock below the reorder point, When the daily sweep runs, Then a reorder suggestion is generated sized to par and adjusted for the next two weeks' scheduled case mix.
* **AC-I-06-2** — Given a lot expiring within 90 or 30 days, When each threshold is crossed, Then the materials manager is notified once per threshold.

### US-I-07 — Cost per case (Could, 5)

* **AC-I-07-1** — Given completed cases, When the monthly report runs, Then cost per case is reported by procedure and by physician, combining supply usage, staff time and anaesthesia.
* **AC-I-07-2** — Given a preference card whose actual usage diverges from its contents by more than a configured margin, When the report runs, Then the card is flagged for review.

### US-I-08 — Equipment availability for scheduling (Must, 3)

* **AC-I-08-1** — Given a case requiring a scope type, When booking occurs, Then availability at that time is checked against the scope register.
* **AC-I-08-2** — Given no instance will be available, When booking is attempted, Then a warning is shown with the conflicting case.

## 16. EP-J — Coding and charge capture

REQ-14. Eight stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open questions 2 and 4** (CPT licence, professional claim scope). Every story here needs review by a certified coder before it enters a sprint.

### US-J-01 — Derive codes from documentation (Must, 8)

* **AC-J-01-1** — Given a signed procedure note with structured findings, When coding runs, Then procedure codes derive from the performed procedures and findings, never from the scheduled procedure.
* **AC-J-01-2** — Given a case scheduled as screening where a polypectomy was performed, When coding runs, Then the polypectomy code is produced.
* **AC-J-01-3** — Given an unsigned note, When coding is attempted, Then it is refused.

### US-J-02 — Screening-to-diagnostic conversion (Must, 8)

* **AC-J-02-1** — Given a case, When coding runs, Then the system determines from the referral and documented indication whether the intent was screening or diagnostic, independent of the CPT code.
* **AC-J-02-2** — Given screening intent, an intervention performed, and a Medicare payer, When coding runs, Then modifier PT is applied.
* **AC-J-02-3** — Given screening intent, an intervention performed, and a commercial payer, When coding runs, Then modifier 33 is applied per the configured payer rule.
* **AC-J-02-4** — Given the payer rule for that payer is not configured, When coding runs, Then no modifier is guessed and a work item is raised for the coder.
* **AC-J-02-5** — Given a conversion occurred, When the patient estimate is revisited, Then the change in patient responsibility is flagged.

### US-J-03 — Multiple endoscopy rule (Must, 8)

* **AC-J-03-1** — Given several endoscopic procedures in one session, When coding runs, Then the system identifies which fall in the same endoscopic family.
* **AC-J-03-2** — Given two or more procedures in the same family, When coding runs, Then the highest-valued procedure is sequenced first and the rule is applied to the remainder with the appropriate modifier.
* **AC-J-03-3** — Given procedures in different families, When coding runs, Then the multiple endoscopy rule is not applied.
* **AC-J-03-4** — Given the family table, When it is updated, Then already-finalized cases retain the sequencing they were coded with and the table version is recorded on each case.

### US-J-04 — Distinct site modifiers (Must, 5)

* **AC-J-04-1** — Given the same procedure performed at distinct anatomical sites, When coding runs, Then modifier 59 or the payer's X-modifier is applied.
* **AC-J-04-2** — Given the anatomical sites come from the structured findings, When any finding lacks a site, Then no distinct-site modifier is applied and a work item is raised.

### US-J-05 — Diagnosis coding and sequencing (Must, 5)

* **AC-J-05-1** — Given a documented indication and findings, When coding runs, Then ICD-10-CM codes are produced with an explicit primary.
* **AC-J-05-2** — Given a screening case, When coding runs, Then the screening Z-code is primary even when a polyp is found.
* **AC-J-05-3** — Given family history is documented, When coding runs, Then the family history code is included.

### US-J-06 — Code rationale (Must, 5)

* **AC-J-06-1** — Given any suggested code, When presented, Then it carries the code, modifier set, the finding or note passage supporting it, the rule applied and a confidence level.
* **AC-J-06-2** — Given a suggestion whose supporting documentation cannot be identified, When coding completes, Then the suggestion is withheld and a work item is raised.
* **AC-J-06-3** — Given a payer audit request, When a case's coding is exported, Then the rationale for every code is included.

### US-J-07 — Physician or coder approval gate (Must, 5)

* **AC-J-07-1** — Given suggested codes, When claim build is attempted without approval, Then it is refused.
* **AC-J-07-2** — Given approval, When recorded, Then approver identity, role and timestamp are stored.
* **AC-J-07-3** — Given an approval screen, When it loads, Then items needing judgment are surfaced first and changing a code requires no more steps than accepting one.
* **AC-J-07-4** — Given any agent, When it attempts to approve codes, Then it is refused under every configuration.

### US-J-08 — Facility and professional charge sets (Must, 5)

* **AC-J-08-1** — Given an approved code set, When charges are generated, Then facility and professional charges are produced as distinct sets.
* **AC-J-08-2** — Given the facility charge set, When priced, Then the ASC payment system's covered-procedures list and payment indicators are applied.
* **AC-J-08-3** — Given separately billable supplies, When the payer's rules permit, Then they are added to the facility charge set.
* **AC-J-08-4** — Given anaesthesia was provided, When charges are generated, Then anaesthesia time units are recorded and made available for export.

## 17. EP-K — Claims and revenue cycle

REQ-15. Eleven stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open question 6** (clearinghouse) and dependent on payer EDI enrolment, which is administrative and on the critical path.

![claim lifecycle · 11 states, 2 exception paths](data:image/png;base64,)

claim lifecycle · 11 states, 2 exception paths

### US-K-01 — Build the claim (Must, 8)

* **AC-K-01-1** — Given approved charges, When the claim is built, Then it carries facility NPI and tax ID, patient and subscriber demographics, coverage, place of service 24, procedure codes with modifiers and units, diagnosis codes in sequence, authorization number where present, charges, and rendering and referring provider identifiers.
* **AC-K-01-2** — Given the payer's required format, When the claim is built, Then 837I or 837P is produced accordingly.

### US-K-02 — Scrub before submission (Must, 8)

* **AC-K-02-1** — Given a built claim, When the scrub runs, Then it validates required fields, code and modifier combinations, diagnosis-to-procedure support, authorization presence and validity on the service date, demographic agreement with the eligibility response, and service date inside the coverage period.
* **AC-K-02-2** — Given any scrub failure, When it occurs, Then the claim is not submitted and a work item names the failing check.
* **AC-K-02-3** — Given a scrub failure, When any automated path is attempted, Then no configuration permits auto-submission of a failing claim.

### US-K-03 — Submit and track acknowledgements (Must, 8)

* **AC-K-03-1** — Given a clean claim, When submitted, Then the submission is recorded with timestamp and clearinghouse reference.
* **AC-K-03-2** — Given a 999 rejecting the file, When received, Then the administrator is alerted immediately and every claim in that file is marked not submitted.
* **AC-K-03-3** — Given a 277CA, When received, Then the claim moves to accepted or rejected with the payer's reason.
* **AC-K-03-4** — Given a claim with no 277CA after the configured window, When the sweep runs, Then it is escalated as potentially lost.

### US-K-04 — Post remittance (Must, 8)

* **AC-K-04-1** — Given an 835, When parsed, Then payment, contractual adjustment, and patient responsibility split into deductible, coinsurance and copay are posted.
* **AC-K-04-2** — Given a denial line, When parsed, Then CARC and RARC codes are stored.
* **AC-K-04-3** — Given a contracted rate exists for the procedure and payer, When payment posts, Then it is compared and any underpayment is flagged.

### US-K-05 — Denial worklist (Must, 5)

* **AC-K-05-1** — Given a denial, When posted, Then a work item is created categorized as eligibility, authorization, medical necessity, coding, timely filing, duplicate, coordination of benefits or bundling.
* **AC-K-05-2** — Given a category, When the work item opens, Then its defined work path is presented.
* **AC-K-05-3** — Given any denial, When it is reviewed, Then acceptance of the denial requires a human action and is never automated.

### US-K-06 — Appeal deadlines (Must, 3)

* **AC-K-06-1** — Given a denial and the payer's appeal window, When the work item is created, Then the deadline is computed and stored.
* **AC-K-06-2** — Given an appeal deadline within the configured warning period, When the sweep runs, Then it escalates.
* **AC-K-06-3** — Given a deadline passes unactioned, When it passes, Then it is recorded as a lost appeal and reported monthly.

### US-K-07 — Feed denial patterns upstream (Should, 3)
