* **AC-K-07-1** — Given three authorization denials for one payer and procedure within 90 days, When the pattern is detected, Then the administrator is alerted that the auth matrix may be wrong, naming the combination.

### US-K-08 — Secondary claims (Should, 5)

* **AC-K-08-1** — Given primary adjudication and a secondary coverage on file, When the 835 posts, Then a secondary claim is generated carrying the primary's adjudication.

### US-K-09 — Patient statements (Must, 5)

* **AC-K-09-1** — Given a remaining patient balance, When a statement is generated, Then services are described in plain language rather than by code alone.
* **AC-K-09-2** — Given an amount under appeal, When statements run, Then that amount is excluded and the patient is not billed for it.
* **AC-K-09-3** — Given a statement, When the patient pays online or enrols in a plan, Then the balance updates and the collections path pauses.

### US-K-10 — Daily operational report (Must, 3)

* **AC-K-10-1** — Given a completed day, When the report runs, Then charges entered, claims submitted, cash posted and denials received are reported.

### US-K-11 — Monthly RCM report (Must, 5)

* **AC-K-11-1** — Given a completed month, When the report runs, Then days in AR, clean claim rate, first-pass resolution rate, denial rate by category and payer, net collection rate and AR aging buckets are reported.
* **AC-K-11-2** — Given the report, When exported, Then it is in a format the center's accountant can use.

## 18. EP-L — Quality, QAPI and recall

REQ-16 and REQ-17. Ten stories. **Blocked by REQ-22 open questions 1 and 7** (accreditor, result-communication policy).

If EP-F and EP-G captured their timestamps and structured findings correctly, almost everything here is reporting. If they did not, this epic becomes permanent manual chart abstraction.

### US-L-01 — Operational metrics (Must, 5)

* **AC-L-01-1** — Given completed cases, When the operational report runs, Then first-case on-time start rate, turnover time by room, block utilization, cancellation rate by reason, same-day cancellation rate, PACU length of stay and schedule accuracy by physician and procedure are computed from stage timestamps.
* **AC-L-01-2** — Given no manual entry occurs, When the report runs, Then every metric derives from recorded transitions.

### US-L-02 — GI clinical quality measures (Must, 8)

* **AC-L-02-1** — Given screening colonoscopies in patients aged 45 and over with linked pathology, When adenoma detection rate is computed per physician, Then the numerator counts cases with at least one adenoma on pathology.
* **AC-L-02-2** — Given colonoscopies, When cecal intubation rate is computed, Then only cases with a labelled landmark image count as complete.
* **AC-L-02-3** — Given negative screening colonoscopies, When withdrawal time is reported, Then both the mean and the proportion at six minutes or more are produced.
* **AC-L-02-4** — Given Boston scores, When adequate preparation rate is computed, Then the configured adequacy threshold is applied.
* **AC-L-02-5** — Given documented intervals and the guideline table, When concordance is computed, Then the proportion matching guideline is reported with the overrides listed.
* **AC-L-02-6** — Given complications, When reported, Then perforation, post-polypectomy bleeding and unplanned transfer rates are computed within their defined windows.
* **AC-L-02-7** — Given the measures, When the physician dashboard loads, Then they are shown per physician and refreshed nightly.

### US-L-03 — ASCQR capture and submission (Must, 8)

* **AC-L-03-1** — Given the configured program-year measure set, When a case completes, Then the data elements each measure needs are captured without additional manual entry.
* **AC-L-03-2** — Given measure definitions are configuration, When CMS changes the set, Then no code change is required to add or retire a measure.
* **AC-L-03-3** — Given a reporting period, When the submission is produced, Then it is exportable in the format CMS requires.

### US-L-04 — Incident reporting (Must, 5)

* **AC-L-04-1** — Given an incident, When reported, Then date and time, case if applicable, type, people involved, description, immediate action, harm level and state-reportability are recorded.
* **AC-L-04-2** — Given a state-reportable incident, When saved, Then the submission deadline is computed and tracked.
* **AC-L-04-3** — Given any role including administrator, When deletion of an incident is attempted, Then it is refused.
* **AC-L-04-4** — Given a hospital transfer recorded in US-F-12, When it occurs, Then an incident is opened automatically.

### US-L-05 — QAPI program (Must, 5)

* **AC-L-05-1** — Given a quality measure and target, When defined, Then performance against it is tracked over time.
* **AC-L-05-2** — Given a performance improvement project, When recorded with aim, interventions and results, Then it is retrievable as survey evidence.
* **AC-L-05-3** — Given QAPI meetings, When minutes and attendance are recorded, Then they attach to the program record.
* **AC-L-05-4** — Given a surveyor request, When the QAPI pack is exported, Then measures, projects, minutes and incident summaries are included.

### US-L-06 — Compute the surveillance interval (Must, 8)

* **AC-L-06-1** — Given findings and pathology, When the interval is computed, Then adenoma count, size, histology including villous features and high-grade dysplasia, piecemeal removal, sessile serrated lesions, prep adequacy, completeness to cecum and family history are all inputs.
* **AC-L-06-2** — Given inadequate prep or an incomplete examination, When the interval is computed, Then the early-repeat rule is applied before the findings-based rule.
* **AC-L-06-3** — Given a recommendation, When produced, Then the guideline table version that produced it is recorded.
* **AC-L-06-4** — Given a recommendation, When presented, Then it is never applied without physician confirmation.
* **AC-L-06-5** — Given a physician override, When saved, Then a reason is required and the override appears in QAPI review.

### US-L-07 — Recall register (Must, 5)

* **AC-L-07-1** — Given a confirmed interval, When saved, Then the patient enters the recall register with due date, indication, physician and the finding that drove it.
* **AC-L-07-2** — Given the register, When queried, Then patients due in the next 90 days and overdue by bucket are returned.

### US-L-08 — Recall outreach (Must, 5)

* **AC-L-08-1** — Given a due date, When the ladder runs, Then contacts are attempted at 90 and 30 days before, at due, and at 30, 90 and 180 days overdue.
* **AC-L-08-2** — Given a patient's channel preference, When outreach runs, Then it escalates from message to letter to phone call.
* **AC-L-08-3** — Given each attempt, When made, Then channel, date, outcome and any response are recorded.
* **AC-L-08-4** — Given a patient who declines, When recorded, Then active outreach stops and they remain in the register with the decline date.

### US-L-09 — Pathology-driven interval reopening (Must, 5)

* **AC-L-09-1** — Given a pathology result that materially differs from the endoscopic impression after an interval was set, When it is acknowledged, Then a work item reopens the interval decision for the physician.
* **AC-L-09-2** — Given such a case, When the interval is reopened, Then the system never adjusts the interval silently.

### US-L-10 — Recall forecasting (Could, 3)

* **AC-L-10-1** — Given the register, When the capacity report runs, Then recall volume is projected 12 months out by month.
* **AC-L-10-2** — Given outreach history, When conversion is reported, Then the rate from outreach to scheduled case is shown by channel.

## 19. EP-M — AI agent layer and guardrails

REQ-18. Nine stories. These ship alongside the epic each agent automates, never ahead of it. The manual path must work first.

### US-M-01 — Agent action framework (Must, 8)

As an architect I want one mechanism for all agent work so that agent and human activity are auditable the same way.

* **AC-M-01-1** — Given an agent performs work, When it does, Then it creates and resolves work items through the same model humans use.
* **AC-M-01-2** — Given any agent action, When executed, Then an audit event records the agent name, model version, prompt version, inputs acted on and the change made.
* **AC-M-01-3** — Given an administrator asks why a case holds a given state, When they open its history, Then the agent, rule, version and timestamp that produced it are shown.

### US-M-02 — Confidence thresholds and abstention (Must, 8)

* **AC-M-02-1** — Given an agent output below its configured task threshold, When produced, Then the agent abstains and creates a work item instead of acting.
* **AC-M-02-2** — Given abstention, When it occurs, Then it is recorded as a normal outcome, not as an error.
* **AC-M-02-3** — Given agent metrics, When reported, Then abstention rate is reported alongside accuracy and treated as a success measure.
* **AC-M-02-4** — Given a threshold, When an administrator changes it, Then the change is versioned and audited.

### US-M-03 — Enforce the commit boundary (Must, 8)

As a physician I want the system incapable of committing clinical decisions so that automation cannot exceed its remit.

* **AC-M-03-1** — Given any agent, When it attempts to sign or attest to a clinical document, Then it is refused.
* **AC-M-03-2** — Given any agent, When it attempts to approve codes, set a surveillance interval, accept a payer denial, waive a readiness check, communicate an abnormal result, advise on medication, write off a balance, merge patient records, or pass a hard gate, Then each is refused.
* **AC-M-03-3** — Given the refusals above, When any configuration, setting or role is applied, Then none of them can be enabled.
* **AC-M-03-4** — Given a refusal, When it occurs, Then it is logged with the agent and the attempted action.

### US-M-04 — Degraded-input behaviour (Must, 8)

* **AC-M-04-1** — Given a payer response silent rather than negative on the requested service, When the agent processes it, Then it produces response incomplete and abstains.
* **AC-M-04-2** — Given a transcript with a garbled or inaudible clinical value, When drafting runs, Then the field is empty and flagged.
* **AC-M-04-3** — Given a poorly scanned insurance card, When extraction runs, Then low-confidence fields are empty and flagged.
* **AC-M-04-4** — Given the evaluation harness, When built, Then it is built around degraded inputs, not clean ones.

### US-M-05 — Intake agent (Must, 5)

Automates US-B-02, US-B-03, US-B-04. Commits classification and extraction; never commits a patient match.

* **AC-M-05-1** — Given an incoming item, When the agent runs, Then it classifies and extracts without human initiation.
* **AC-M-05-2** — Given a match candidate below exact, When the agent runs, Then it proposes and stops.

### US-M-06 — Clearance agent (Must, 5)

Automates US-D-01, US-D-03, US-D-04, US-D-05, US-D-06. Commits eligibility results and auth submissions; never accepts a denial.

* **AC-M-06-1** — Given a booked case, When the agent runs, Then eligibility, benefits, auth determination, packet assembly and submission occur without human initiation.
* **AC-M-06-2** — Given a denial or an incomplete response, When received, Then the agent creates a work item and takes no further action.

### US-M-07 — Outreach agent (Must, 5)

Automates US-E-06, US-E-07, US-L-08. Commits messages and calls; never gives medical advice.

* **AC-M-07-1** — Given a scheduled outreach item, When due, Then the agent contacts the patient through their preferred channel and records the outcome.
* **AC-M-07-2** — Given any generated patient message, When produced, Then it contains no instruction to stop, start or change a medication.
* **AC-M-07-3** — Given a patient response the agent cannot handle, When received, Then it escalates to a named human role.

### US-M-08 — Scribe and coding agents (Must, 5)

Automate US-G-05 and US-J-01 through US-J-06. Neither commits.

* **AC-M-08-1** — Given a completed case, When the scribe runs, Then it produces a draft and stops.
* **AC-M-08-2** — Given a signed note, When the coding agent runs, Then it produces suggestions with rationale and stops.

### US-M-09 — Pre-go-live agent evaluation (Must, 5)

As an administrator I want each agent evaluated before it touches a real patient so that the center can defend its use.

* **AC-M-09-1** — Given an agent, When it is proposed for production, Then a written evaluation exists covering what it does, its failure modes, its test set, measured accuracy, abstention rate and the human control.
* **AC-M-09-2** — Given no such evaluation, When the agent is enabled for real patients, Then it is refused.
* **AC-M-09-3** — Given the evaluations, When the QAPI pack is exported, Then they are included.

## 20. Non-functional acceptance criteria

These apply to every story. They are part of the Definition of Done in section 4 and are not optional per-story extras.

| ID | Criterion | How it is verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NFR-1 | Any screen loads within 1 second at p95 | Automated performance test in CI |
| NFR-2 | Any save of a clinical action in the room completes within 500 ms at p95 | Automated performance test |
| NFR-3 | Document upload and extraction completes within 60 seconds | Automated test against the fixture library |
| NFR-4 | Every PHI read and write emits an audit event | Integration test asserting the event |
| NFR-5 | Access control is enforced server-side, verified with a user who should be denied | Negative-path test per story |
| NFR-6 | No PHI appears in logs, URLs, error messages or analytics | Automated scan plus review |
| NFR-7 | All data in transit uses TLS 1.3; all data at rest is encrypted | Infrastructure test |
| NFR-8 | Session terminates after 15 minutes idle on clinical workstations | Automated test |
| NFR-9 | Every interactive element is keyboard reachable with a visible focus state | Automated accessibility check |
| NFR-10 | Patient-facing surfaces meet WCAG 2.1 AA | Automated check plus manual review |
| NFR-11 | Clinical screens are legible and operable at arm's length, with 44 px minimum touch targets | Manual review on the target device |
| NFR-12 | Every screen has a designed empty state and a designed error state | Review |
| NFR-13 | Errors state what happened and what to do, never a raw exception | Review |
| NFR-14 | Work in progress survives interruption and navigation away | Automated test |
| NFR-15 | No test, fixture or seed uses real patient data in any environment | CI check |
| NFR-16 | Every external interface defines its unreachable behaviour, queue depth, alert threshold and manual fallback | Documented per interface |
| NFR-17 | Backups restore successfully | Quarterly restore test |
| NFR-18 | Patient-facing content is available in Spanish | Review |

### Severity definitions for support

Agree these before go-live; they belong in the agreement with the center.

| Severity | Definition | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Procedures are stopped or patient safety is affected | Minutes, during operating hours |
| 2 | A core workflow is unavailable but a workaround exists | 1 hour |
| 3 | A non-core function is broken | 1 business day |
| 4 | Cosmetic or an enhancement request | Next release |

### Environments

Three: local development, staging with synthetic data only, and production. Staging mirrors production configuration. No path exists from production to staging for patient data, and no exception to that is granted for debugging.

### Hard gates — the list that must never regress

When a refactor touches any of these, the test for it must still pass. Add each to a protected suite:

* ☐ Gate 1: identity, consent, H&P before pre-op (AC-F-02-1)
* ☐ Gate 2: anaesthesia, anticoagulation, equipment, escort before the room (AC-F-06-1)
* ☐ Consent and identity cannot be waived by any role (AC-D-12-4, AC-F-02-3)
* ☐ Timeout required before procedure start (AC-F-05-3)
* ☐ Scope reprocessing gate has no override (AC-I-05-4)
* ☐ Signed documents are immutable (AC-G-03-3)
* ☐ Physician or coder approval before claim build (AC-J-07-1)
* ☐ No agent can sign, approve codes, or pass a hard gate (AC-M-03-2, AC-M-03-3)
* ☐ Scrub failure never auto-submits (AC-K-02-3)
* ☐ Specimen count reconciles before case closure (AC-H-02-2)
* ☐ No patient auto-created or auto-merged (AC-B-05-4)
* ☐ Audit events cannot be altered (AC-A-09-3)

### Document status

Draft. Story IDs are stable; estimates and priorities are a first pass and should be re-estimated by whoever builds them. Clinical, coding and regulatory stories need review by someone with current credentials before they enter a sprint. Approximately 130 stories against the capacity note in section 3.
